name: Facet
text: Adopt a persistent dark theme with a manual light-mode toggle that remembers the user’s choice. Dark themes reduce eye strain in low light and improve focus on data, aligning with our goal of clarity and liveliness. The trade-off is slightly higher battery drain on OLED screens, but the visibility and enjoyment gains outweigh it. A manual toggle respects user preference without cluttering the interface.

name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t just battery drain—it’s *habituation failure*. Users will toggle light mode in bright rooms, then forget to switch back, creating inconsistency fatigue. A better alternative: default to system preference, but let the graph’s data density dictate contrast—high-density graphs stay dark, low-density allow light mode. Settle it with A/B tests measuring task completion speed and user-reported strain after a week.

name: Facet
text:
We should default to the system's dark mode preference and adjust contrast based on graph data density. This approach ensures consistency with the user's overall interface experience, reducing cognitive friction, and allows for optimal visibility of complex data. By doing this, we accept the trade-off of potentially reduced control over the look and feel of our interface, but gain a more seamless and intuitive user experience. This decision prioritizes clarity and liveliness, aligning with our goal of creating an enjoyable and effective visualization interface.

name: Pane
text: The real risk here isn’t just cognitive friction—it’s *habituation failure* in reverse. Users will toggle to light mode in bright rooms, then forget to switch back to dark, leaving the graph in a low-contrast state that hurts readability. Settle this by testing two defaults: system preference vs. high-contrast dark. Measure which one users stick with after 24 hours in varied lighting.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Default to system preference for dark mode, but override to high-contrast dark when graph data density exceeds a threshold—with a one-time manual override that persists until the next system preference change.

Result: A dark-themed interface that adapts contrast for dense data while preventing habituation fatigue. Owned by Facet (visualization-w1).
